clusters.title: The Release signing paragraph names an operator-held credential that signs release artifacts, but no page says what is signed, how, where it is published or how a user verifies it; S1, J1 step 2, B1 and 10 10.2 know only checksums.txt and the provenance attestation, and S1 calls the attestation the signature.
clusters.scenario: v1.0.0 ships with checksums.txt and an attestation; the operator never signs anything because no step asks; a user runs J1 step 2, every proof passes, and the control ADR 0008 decision 6 relies on against a token-driven release was never applied.
clusters.change: Decide one of two texts and write it in 05 5.4, S1, J1 step 2, 11 11.2 B1 and 10 10.2 Release and bootstrap together. (a) Recommended: v1 publishes no signature beyond the provenance attestation. Replace the Release signing paragraph with: "v1 releases carry checksums.txt and a keyless build provenance attestation and no other signature; the attestation proves that release.yml built the archive, not that the maintainer approved the release." Add a Deferred decisions row "an operator signature over checksums.txt, made outside GitHub; until then the attestation is the only release proof; reopened by the first release whose tag the maintainer did not push, a second contributor, or the token narrowing of ADR 0008". Remove "signed" from S1's evidence wording. Reword ADR 0008 decision 6 to match. (b) Name the signed object (checksums.txt), the tool and key type, the published verifying key and fingerprint (README, SECURITY.md), the operator step in 10 10.2, the verify command in J1 step 2, an S1 evidence item and a B1 predicate.
clusters.cost: A maintainer decision; (a) about sixty words removed, one deferred row, a superseding sentence for ADR 0008 decision 6; (b) a tool, a key, an operator step per release and one J1 command.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend (a): delete the Release signing paragraph, state that the attestation is the only release proof and what it does not prove, add the deferred row with its trigger, and reword ADR 0008 decision 6 in a short superseding record. (b) adds a key to keep and an operator step per release for a control no second user needs yet.
clusters.operator_reason: Changes ADR 0008 decision 6 (a decision record) and the release trust 05 5.4 accepts; the choice between a signing step and none is the maintainer's.

clusters.title: The default-branch ruleset is said to require a code-owner review in 05 5.3, 05 5.4, 10 10.2 item a, 12 12.4 and 12 12.9 while the same cells say that, as measured on 2026-10-08, it requires none; the spec describes the removed gate several times and the gate that exists nowhere.
clusters.scenario: A contributor or the implementer of T005 reads 05 5.3 or the 12 12.4 merge row, believes an independent review guards ask-first paths, and builds or documents a review step that does not exist; a sandbox session merges its own surface change through the API and nothing refuses it.
clusters.change: In 05 5.4 rewrite the approval-line row to state the merge gate as it is, once: "The default-branch ruleset requires CI green and refuses a direct push to the default branch; it requires no review (measured 2026-10-08, ADR 0008). The approval line, checked by tools/ci pr, is the only recorded approval, and it is typed by the PR's author." In 05 5.3 replace "the ruleset that requires the code-owner review" with "the ruleset's requirements" and add "what this approval is worth with one account is in 05 5.4". In 10 10.2 item a, the 12 12.4 merge row and 12 12.9, delete the sentence stating the review requirement and its "as measured" patch and write "the merge requirements, and what they are worth, are in 05 5.4". Keep the earlier configuration in docs/reviews and ADR 0008 only.

Change the ADR 0008 narrowing trigger to "the first issue or PR from an account other than the operator's".
clusters.cost: One row, one clause, one working rule in 12 12.9, one trigger change in ADR 0008 (a follow-up record).

clusters.title: The token row accepts merges, v* tags and ruleset edits as process only, and the spec does not weigh the cheap deterministic guard against mistakes: a julieta-claude PreToolUse refusal of gh pr merge, a v* tag push and ruleset API calls.

clusters.title: The token row rests on two duties held in memory (reading the security log at each sitting, a review every 2 autonomous work sessions that nobody counts), and its release-candidate trigger makes the token decision due just before block B.

clusters.resolution_text: Recommend the counted-PR trigger and the C7 checkpoint as written.
clusters.operator_reason: It changes the triggers of an accepted risk and of ADR 0008.

clusters.title: I17 and 10 10.1 inject faults into the promotion commit only; no test kills romeu after each step of salvage, rm, recreate or retire, so "holds under a kill at any line" is unmeasured for the machine that protects work.
clusters.scenario: An implementation writes closed-removed before sbx env rm; a kill between the two leaves a live sandbox romeu no longer recognizes, and every CI level stays green.
clusters.change: Add to I17's Test cell and to 10 10.1's Additional required tests a row "Destructive-command fault injection": a test hook kills romeu after each step of salvage, rm, recreate and retire; the next run, salvage or rm converges, no salvage record says lost after a complete one, and sbx env rm is never reached without a complete or accepted record of this generation.
clusters.cost: A test seam, one e2e table, a mid-session kill in the fake sbx.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as written.

clusters.title: I28 claims romeu parses descriptors the way sbx does, but the conformance fixtures are recorded once against one sbx and one frontend and nothing re-runs them when a pin moves.
clusters.scenario: A newer sbx widens what a capability key grants; gate 2 still shows the old meaning, and the operator approves a wider capability than shown.
clusters.change: In I28 and 06 6.1: the conformance fixtures record the sbx version and frontend digest they were made with; a frontend pin change, or an sbx version entering the tested window, requires the A11 and A12 conformance subset again, named in the PR's Evidence.
clusters.cost: One rule and two recorded fields.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as written.

clusters.title: The admitted-call-site table of the I16, I31 and I32 scans lives under tools/ci, so each package that legitimately removes a temp file edits the gate's code and needs a checks approval.
clusters.scenario: T039 and T064 each add functions to the one table and both PRs need a checks approval for data about their own package.
clusters.change: No mechanism change: add to 05 5.2 under the scans "an admitted call site widens I16, I31 or I32, so the table stays on the checks surface and each admission carries the checks approval line".
clusters.cost: One sentence.
clusters.resolution_text: State the limit; a marker comment in the admitted function would let any PR admit itself without an approval.

clusters.title: Common pre-existing setups (a global sbx GitHub secret, VS Code workspace trust off, an existing ~/dev) are refused at preflight with no fix hint stated.
clusters.scenario: A developer who set the github secret globally, as sbx documents, sees every romeu run exit 2 at preflight step 5 (I22) with a hint the spec does not define.
clusters.change: In the 04 doctor table give each refusing pre check its hint text: the per-project sbx secret command, the VS Code setting to change, and what init does with a non-empty root.
clusters.cost: Hint texts for about five checks.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as written in 04.

clusters.title: romeu pull, the hardened review checkout, both workspace files, I19 and two residual-risk rows exist for a host-side review path the start does not need, and dev.code-workspace is opened by no journey.
clusters.scenario: The first user reviews on GitHub (2.6, ADR 0008); J4 is the one journey for pull and is outside S7's CI set; dev.code-workspace is rewritten on every promotion and retire and carries I13 and I14 with no reader.
clusters.change: Defer romeu pull, the review checkout and review.code-workspace as one row ("until then the PR on GitHub is the review; reopened by the first time the maintainer needs a sandbox branch on the host before it is pushed"); delete dev.code-workspace or give it a journey step; I19 and the two 05 5.4 rows about the review checkout leave with pull.
clusters.cost: Deletions in 01, 02, 04, 05, 09; the plan loses most of T067.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend the deferral with its trigger; it removes a command and two accepted-risk rows.
clusters.operator_reason: It changes the scope (00 0.5) and removes accepted risks from 05 5.4.

clusters.title: The run layout is multiplexer-neutral for non-goal renderers while nothing says what happens if herdr, pre-1.0 with no signed releases, stops being maintained.
clusters.scenario: herdr is on the path of every romeu run; Q16 and 05 5.4 cover churn and provenance, not abandonment; the neutrality is paid now and the event that would use it has no row.
clusters.change: Add a Deferred decisions row "a second run-layout renderer; until then herdr, pinned by version and sha256, is the one renderer; reopened by a herdr release that breaks the protocol number A13 recorded, six months without a herdr release, or a CVE in it". Keep 03 3.2's format; the row now gives its neutrality a trigger.
clusters.cost: One row.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the row; leave 03 3.2 as is.

clusters.title: Commit signing from a dedicated host agent is a product kit with its own surface, setting, check and open question, and no sentence says why the start needs it.
clusters.scenario: A second adopter cannot tell whether to adopt the git-ssh-sign kit or ignore it.
clusters.change: Add to the 06 6.4 git-ssh-sign intro: "it exists because the maintainer signs every commit and runs no agent that cannot; it is opt-in", and mark it opt-in in the README outline.
clusters.cost: Two sentences.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in 06 6.4 rather than 00 0.5, so the scope text does not change.

clusters.title: .github/workflows/release.yml matches the release and dependencies surfaces, so tools/ci pr asks for two approval lines and the overlap is named nowhere.
clusters.scenario: A PR editing release.yml carries a release line and fails pr for the missing dependencies line; the author adds a second line with the same words.
clusters.change: Add under the 05 5.3 list: "A path may match several surfaces; one approval line may name several surface ids, and it covers each."
clusters.cost: One sentence and a small pr clause.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as written.

clusters.title: The dependencies surface lists every path where mise reads its configuration as measured with mise 2026.10.3, and nothing re-measures mise's config discovery when the mise pin moves.
clusters.scenario: A mise bump reads a new config file name; a change adds that file without touching an ask-first surface or tripping hygiene.
clusters.change: Add to 05 5.3 after the dependencies sentence: "a change of the mise pin re-measures config discovery at the new version, named in the PR's Evidence". Add the mise counterpart of the golangci-lint sentence to ADR 0007 Consequences.
clusters.cost: One sentence, one ADR sentence.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the 05 5.3 sentence now; the ADR 0007 sentence goes to the operator with the next decisions batch.

clusters.title: Every ask-first surface has one owner and no contribution path or continuity statement is given for outside contributors.
clusters.scenario: An adopter opens a catalog PR for their stack and no page says who reviews it or when.
clusters.change: Add to 12 12.8's CONTRIBUTING outline one row: "outside PRs to the catalog and kits: the evidence a PR needs; reviewed by the one maintainer, best effort". Add a Deferred decisions row "a second owner for ask-first surfaces; reopened by the first outside PR on a surface".
clusters.cost: One outline row, one deferred row.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as written; no continuity promise beyond what one person can keep.

clusters.title: The first mention of ADR 0008 in 05 is the bare "(ADR 0008)" in the second row of 5.4, before the linked mention, which rule 9 of ADR 0001 fails once its check lands in T086.
clusters.scenario: T086 lands the rule 9 check and tools/ci all goes red on 05-security.md in an unrelated PR late in the plan.
clusters.change: Write the first mention in 05 (row 2 of 5.4, or the threat paragraph if R8-05-5 adds one there) as "[ADR 0008, let the sandbox act as the maintainer on GitHub](../adr/0008-let-the-sandbox-act-as-the-maintainer-on-github.md)"; move the rule 9 matcher over the spec from T086 to T006 in the plan.
clusters.cost: One edit and one plan move.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as written.

clusters.title: docs/spec/** is on no ask-first surface while the spec is the plan's source of truth and tools/ci vocabulary and sequences read its tables, so gate inputs and the security model sit outside the gate.
clusters.scenario: An agent PR edits the Not column of 01 1.7 to make its wording pass tools/ci vocabulary and rewrites a 05 5.4 row in the same change; no approval line is required and it merges.
clusters.change: Add a surface to 05 5.3: "- id: specification / globs: [docs/spec.md, docs/spec/01-system-model.md, docs/spec/05-security.md] / reason: the tables the checks read and the security model". The alternative moves the two tables to data files under tools/ci rendered into the spec.
clusters.cost: Three globs, or two data files and two generator rows.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend the three-file surface: it covers the check inputs and the security model without an approval on every spec edit.
clusters.operator_reason: The maintainer decided in round 3 which documents are surfaces (decision records, check code); adding the spec changes that decision and the approval load.

clusters.title: The threat paragraph trusts "the romeu release (built from reviewed, signed commits, with verified attestations)" while no review is required, commits are signed by the agent's forwarded key, and the attestation proves only that release.yml built the archive.
clusters.scenario: A reader concludes the release is human-reviewed and human-signed; neither holds today, so the host side's trust root is an axiom the text does not support.
clusters.change: Reword to: "The host operator and the romeu release are trusted. A release is what release.yml built from main and attested (10 10.2); what review, commit signatures and the attestation are worth today is in 05 5.4." Make 02 2.1's "one signed-commit release" follow. If R8-05-1 chooses (b), add "and signed by the maintainer".
clusters.cost: Two sentences.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the reword now; it holds under either outcome of the release-signing decision.
